Preferred IV coefficient 3.1488 years per unit increase in natural-log school-age per-pupil spending (district-clustered SE 0.7906; p <0.01; Table III, p. 191). These are reform-based model estimates for the sampled 1955–1985 birth cohorts, not randomized trial effects.
The school-finance model estimated more completed schooling from higher spending for children in its low-income group.

Preferred IV coefficient 4.5899 years per unit increase in natural-log school-age per-pupil spending (district-clustered SE 1.2072; p <0.01; Table III, p. 191). This group had parental family income below twice the poverty line in at least one childhood year.
The school-finance model did not establish that higher spending increased completed schooling for children in its nonpoor group.
